# Sightline release notes

<!-- Generated by build.sh from src/releases.json. Edit that file, not this one. -->

## 1.146.0 · Oct 27, 2026

Empty boxes take one line.

### Improved

- **Updates and Notes stay small until you use them** (Details). Each empty box is one line with Add an update or Add a note. Click it, or press U or S, and the box opens with the cursor in it. A box with updates, notes or a half-written draft shows in full. *Where:* The details panel for an initiative or task

## 1.145.1 · Oct 27, 2026

Clearer help when the page doesn't start.

### Fixed

- **Check a copy on Windows too** (Start-up). It now gives the command for Windows (Get-FileHash in PowerShell), a Mac and Linux, says to compare with the .sha256 file beside it, and says a mismatch means the file changed on the way over: copy it as a file, not by pasting its text. *Where:* The "Sightline didn't start" message
- **The whole message, with nothing over it** (Start-up). Only the message shows, so every step is readable. *Where:* The "Sightline didn't start" message

## 1.145.0 · Oct 27, 2026

A lighter details panel.

### Improved

- **What you need first, the rest folded** (Details). Warnings, status, updates, notes, title, owner, dates and the first three tasks come first. Schedule, Waits for, Organize and More fold away, each with a one-line summary such as "2 weeks". The folds you open are remembered for initiatives and tasks, in this browser. *Where:* Click any initiative or task

## 1.144.0 · Oct 27, 2026

A lighter menu.

### Improved

- **Pin the pages you use, and the rest folds away** (Menu). Your pinned pages sit at the top: Today, Sprint, Timeline and Capacity to start. Groups start closed and show a dot when something inside needs you. Numbers show only when something needs you, such as high risks. Delivery is split into Plan, Review and History. *Where:* The menu on the left. Point at a page and click the pin, or focus it and press P. Up to five, in this browser only.

## 1.143.2 · Oct 27, 2026

Task names stay on screen in Days.

### Fixed

- **Names near the right edge are no longer cut off** (Days). A task name that won't fit to the right of its bar sits to its left instead. If neither side has room, it is shortened with an ellipsis. Milestone names near the edge are shortened the same way. Point at a shortened name to see it in full. *Where:* Days, especially with one initiative open

## 1.143.1 · Oct 27, 2026

No new version without a change.

### Fixed

- **Saving with nothing changed leaves the file alone** (Shared plans). The file only changes when the plan does. Done editing with nothing changed puts the file back exactly as it was before Start editing. Save, and quick updates, with nothing changed write nothing. An edit you changed back counts as nothing. *Where:* Start editing, Save, Done editing, and quick updates on a shared plan

## 1.143.0 · Oct 27, 2026

Old captures show on Today.

### New

- **Captures waiting over 30 days show on Today** (Today). In the Team view, Today lists captures open for over 30 days under Waiting in triage, oldest first, with who asked and how long it's been open. Needs attention counts them. Triage opens one in To triage, to hand it off or decline it. *Where:* Today, Team

## 1.142.0 · Oct 27, 2026

Tasks that start too early are counted.

### Improved

- **Tasks that start too early are in the warning bar** (Timeline). Open tasks that start too early are listed with initiatives in the warning bar, among work that starts before what it waits for finishes. Click a name to open it, or Move them later to fix them all. In Present, Review counts them as starting too early, and stepping through them opens each task. *Where:* The warning bar above the chart, and Review in Present

### Fixed

- **Finished tasks keep their dates** (Timeline). A done task stays on the dates it ran on. Only open work moves. *Where:* Move them later, and automatic moving of linked work

## 1.141.0 · Oct 27, 2026

See only what was added here.

### New

- **Show only work added here** (Timeline). Added here, next to All sources, Jira only and Jira + mine, shows only tasks and initiatives with no Jira key, plus any initiative holding such work. Jira-linked items and Jira's stories are hidden; milestones, gates and notes stay. A banner says so, Present too. It's your own choice, for this plan in this browser. *Where:* Timeline or List, View, Show work from

## 1.140.1 · Oct 27, 2026

Waits-for links merge link by link.

### Fixed

- **Two people adding what something waits for both keep their links** (Shared plans). Both sets of links are kept, and a link one of you removed stays removed. A link that would make work wait for itself through the other person's links isn't merged: theirs wins, yours is backed up, and Sightline tells you which link wasn't kept. *Where:* Saving a shared plan someone else changed

## 1.140.0 · Oct 27, 2026

Line up existing tasks behind what they wait for.

### New

- **Move a task to right after what it waits for** (Assistant). A proposed move can say start after instead of a date. The task starts the working day after the last thing it waits for finishes, skipping weekends, holidays and its owners' time off. It keeps its id and its links. When something it waits for is late and not done, it's refused: give a date. *Where:* Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel

### Fixed

- **Marking existing tasks as guesses no longer conflicts** (Assistant). A task that isn't marked as a guess reads as not a guess, so the change applies. *Where:* Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel

## 1.139.0 · Oct 27, 2026

Order without dates.

### New

- **See the work in order, without dates** (List). By order, in the List, groups work into steps: step 1 waits for nothing, and each later step waits only on earlier ones. Waiting for an initiative means waiting for everything in it. Steps show order, not what's ready. Loops, and waiting and unstaffed rows, are set apart. The Waits on column is now Waits for. *Where:* List, By order

### Improved

- **Capacity says what it doesn't count** (Sprint). Under the capacity table, a line says what the points leave out in those sprints: Jira items with no estimate, and open tasks added here. *Where:* Sprint, Capacity

## 1.138.0 · Oct 27, 2026

Clearer about what's what.

### New

- **Added here, on work Jira doesn't track** (Timeline). In a plan that has Jira work, plan tasks on the Days view and rows in the List that nothing in Jira tracks say Added here. On the Timeline, an initiative with no Jira key says so when you hover it, and the Key explains it. A plan with no Jira work shows no labels. *Where:* Days view, List, and the Timeline's Key

### Improved

- **Moved dates say what they wait for** (Assistant). Each date a proposed change moves later now says what that item waits for, like waits for "Adapter". Holidays, time off and gates can move dates too, so it says what it waits for, not that it moved because of it. *Where:* Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel
- **Apply says what it added** (Assistant). After you apply proposed changes, the status line counts what changed, like 30 tasks added, 29 links added, 12 dates moved. Your assistant reads the same count. *Where:* The status line, after Apply

## 1.137.0 · Oct 27, 2026

Order before dates.

### New

- **Add tasks by what they start after** (Assistant). A proposed task can say what it starts after instead of a date. It starts the working day after the last of those finishes, skipping weekends, holidays and its owners' time off. The review says what each starts after. *Where:* Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel
- **Mark a length as a guess** (Tasks). Length is a guess, on a task's card, hatches the task on the Days view and labels it guess. The initiative's card counts how many of its tasks have guessed lengths. *Where:* A task's card, under its dates
- **Start right after what it waits for** (Tasks). A task that could start sooner says so on its card, with the day and a link to start then. One that starts before what it waits for finishes is flagged on its card and tagged too early on the Days view. The card also says whether it moves later on its own. *Where:* A task's card, under its dates

## 1.136.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Show only some initiatives.

### New

- **Show only one or more initiatives** (Filters). Show only this, on an initiative's card, narrows Timeline, List and Capacity to it, everything inside it and what holds it. Also show this adds more. Milestones done when a shown initiative is stay; gates are hidden. The picks are a filter like the others, so a saved view keeps them. *Where:* An initiative's card, or Filters, Initiatives

## 1.135.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Dates in words.

### New

- **Give dates the way people say them** (Assistant). Any date in a proposed change can be words like tomorrow, +3d, next Friday, 2 weeks ago or next sprint. The review says which date each became, flags one in the past, and says when a task's start moves off a weekend. Apply uses that date. Anything else is refused with the forms that work. *Where:* Your assistant's proposed changes, in the review panel

## 1.134.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Who asked, and what happened since.

### New

- **See captures by who asked, and send them a note** (Roadmap). By asker lists everything each person or group raised, open ones first, then what became of the rest. Copy a note for them copies a short note to send back, saying where each one stands. It names no one else. *Where:* Roadmap, To triage, By asker
- **A meeting recap of what changed** (Roadmap). Meeting recap says what's new, raised again, closed and reopened since your last meeting, and how many are still open, ready to read out or paste. It leaves out who asked unless you tick Say who asked. *Where:* Roadmap, To triage, Meeting recap

## 1.133.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Raised again, not captured twice.

### New

- **Record that a request came up again** (Roadmap). A capture's card lists every later time it was raised: who asked, which meeting and when. Record it adds one, and Remove takes one out. The first ask stays as it was. Plans with these records open read-only in older copies of Sightline, so everyone editing should update first. *Where:* Roadmap, To triage, open a capture: Raised again
- **The capture form offers the one you may already have** (Roadmap). As you type what was raised, the form lists captures with a similar name. Same thing: record it there adds this meeting to that one; Capture keeps it separate. Nothing is merged on its own. *Where:* Add (or A, then C), Capture a request or idea

### Improved

- **To triage shows how often something comes up** (Roadmap). A capture raised more than once says so in its row, like raised 3 times. Hover over it to see when and by whom. *Where:* Roadmap, To triage
- **Your assistant records repeats instead of capturing twice** (Assistant). With the meeting-to-plan skill, a request that matches a capture already in the plan is proposed as raised again on that one. When it isn't sure, it captures it separately and says which one it may repeat. *Where:* Your assistant, meeting-to-plan skill

## 1.132.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Capture in one step.

### New

- **Capture a request or idea in one step, even mid-meeting** (Roadmap). One short form: what was raised, its type, who asked, the workstream, the meeting and its date. Only what was raised is needed; nothing else is guessed. The meeting and date carry over, and Capture and add another keeps the form open. *Where:* Add (or A, then C) and Capture a request or idea; Roadmap, To triage

### Improved

- **The roadmap's add row says what it's for** (Roadmap). The row at the top is New roadmap idea, + Add to the roadmap, for something you might ship. A line under it sends requests and questions someone raised to Capture, so they wait in To triage with who asked. *Where:* Roadmap, top row

## 1.131.2 · Oct 26, 2026

A capture closes one way, and held changes say why.

### Fixed

- **A captured item is either handed off or declined, not both** (Roadmap). Handing off or declining a closed item is refused until it's reopened. If two people close it differently at the same time, its card says both and asks you to reopen it and close it once. *Where:* Roadmap, To triage; the item's card
- **A change that waits for you says the right reason** (Assistant). It says what it does: adds a person, a group or a skill, deletes a workstream or changes a workstream's ID. *Where:* Assistant review (Changes)

## 1.131.1 · Oct 26, 2026

Tags on short bars show whole or not at all.

### Fixed

- **A late or +1 tag is never cut off on a short bar** (Timeline). A tag shows whole, or not at all when the bar is too short for it. Late bars keep their red outline, and screen readers still hear late and every owner. *Where:* Timeline, Weeks and Fit

## 1.131.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Capture what comes up in meetings.

### New

- **Capture requests, ideas, gaps and questions, and triage them** (Roadmap). A roadmap item can be captured as a request, idea, process gap or question, with who asked, the meeting's date and its source. To triage lists open captures by workstream, oldest first. Hand one off to an initiative or a Jira issue, or decline it with a reason; neither marks anything done. *Where:* Roadmap, To triage; the item's card

### Improved

- **Assistants can capture from meeting notes, and new people and groups always wait for you** (Assistant). Your assistant can capture each item from your meeting notes with who asked. A new person, group or skill always waits for your review, whatever it may do on its own. *Where:* Connect assistant; the meeting-to-plan skill

## 1.130.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Ask any assistant about your plan.

### New

- **Instructions any assistant can follow to analyze your plan** (Assistant). Analyze with any assistant copies read-only instructions for Copilot, ChatGPT or any other assistant, copies them together with the plan's data for one that can't read files, or saves them as AGENTS.md to put beside your plan. Notes are left out, and nothing is changed. *Where:* Connect assistant, then Analyze with any assistant

## 1.129.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Assistants see what each change does.

### Improved

- **Every change an assistant can propose comes with a plain description** (Assistant). Each change in the context file now has a one-line description of what it does. The planning skills tell the assistant to choose by that description and use the arguments exactly. *Where:* The assistant folder's context file, and the bundled planning skills

## 1.128.1 · Oct 26, 2026

Owner initials stay clear of names.

### Fixed

- **Three-letter owner initials no longer cover the name on a short bar** (Timeline). Three-letter initials are set slightly smaller, and the circle on a bar never grows past its space, so the name always stops before it. *Where:* Weeks and Days, on Jira stories and tasks

## 1.128.0 · Oct 26, 2026

See who owns each Jira item at a glance.

### New

- **Owner initials on every Jira item** (Jira). Every Jira item shows its owner as a small circle with their initials, at the right end of bars and on tiles, cards, List rows and details. A dashed empty circle means unassigned; an outlined one is an owner outside the team. Hover for the full name. People who share initials get a third letter. No pictures are fetched. *Where:* Timeline (Weeks and Days), sprint shelves, Cards, List, and the details panel

### Improved

- **Spotlight rings the person's circles** (Timeline). With Spotlight on from the Show menu, that person's owner circles get a ring wherever they appear, so their work stands out on bars as well as on the shelves. *Where:* Timeline, Show menu, Spotlight

## 1.127.0 · Oct 26, 2026

List shows workstreams.

### New

- **A By workstream layout** (List). By workstream shows each workstream in its Timeline order, with its color, its initiatives and their tasks under it, and a count. List now opens this way unless you picked a different layout on this plan before; choose By initiative once and List remembers it. Copy as table keeps the groups. Everything by start date is now called By start date. *Where:* List, the layout buttons at the top
- **A Workstream column** (List). Every row now says which workstream it's in, on screen and in Copy as table. By workstream leaves the column out, since each group already names it. Like the other columns, you can resize it or set it to wrap. *Where:* List, between Item and Owner

## 1.126.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Names stay in view as you scroll the timeline.

### Improved

- **Bars keep their names when their start is off the screen** (Timeline). A bar's name rides along the left edge of the chart for as long as any of the bar shows. Where only part of the bar is on screen, the name is shortened with an ellipsis inside the bar and never covers the next one. Hover or a screen reader still gives the whole name. *Where:* Timeline, in Weeks, zoomed to a few sprints
- **Milestone, gate and stretch labels follow too** (Timeline). When a milestone, gate or stretch marker is just off to the left, its label stays at the left edge with ‹ in place of the marker, until its own space scrolls away. Printing shows every label where it starts. *Where:* Timeline, in Weeks and Days

## 1.125.3 · Oct 26, 2026

Jira stories stay with their epic when the epic has a parent.

### Fixed

- **Stories group under their epic, not the initiative above it** (Jira). Stories group under their epic again, the same as when the epic isn't linked in the plan. After you update, some stories move from the loose list and the initiative's group into their epic's group. Nothing in the plan file changes. An epic inside another epic still rolls up to the top epic. *Where:* Work, Sort Jira work, and the In a sprint, not on the board list

## 1.125.2 · Oct 26, 2026

The side panel stays where you were.

### Fixed

- **Buttons in the side panel no longer jump it back to the top** (Side panel). The panel stays where you were after a click. Opening a different item still starts at the top. *Where:* The panel on the right: the planning assistant, and any item you open

## 1.125.1 · Oct 26, 2026

Calmer story shelves on the timeline.

### Improved

- **Zoomed in, only the sprints on screen open** (Timeline). Only the sprints in view show tiles; the rest stay as one-line summaries. Click a summary, or the button beside the label, to open them all. Stories with no sprint sit on their own strip under the sprints. *Where:* Timeline, This sprint or This + next
- **Spotlight is one choice for the whole chart** (Timeline). Pick a person once, under Spotlight a person in the Show menu, and their stories stay lit on every shelf while the rest dim. Each name shows how many stories they have, and each shelf's label gives their count there. *Where:* Timeline, Show, then Spotlight a person
- **What tile sizes mean is in the Key** (Timeline). The note that tiles are sized by points, and that a tile's place in a sprint says nothing about when, is said once, in the Key, instead of beside every shelf. *Where:* Timeline, Key

### Fixed

- **Story shelf labels fit in two short lines** (Timeline). The label reads Jira and the story count, then points, done and not estimated on a second line. Hover it for the whole summary; screen readers hear all of it. A small button beside it switches between tiles and summaries. A shelf with nothing on screen takes one line. *Where:* Timeline, in Weeks, by workstream

## 1.125.0 · Oct 26, 2026

Cards: the plan's Jira work, by workstream.

### New

- **A Cards page for the plan's Jira work** (Cards). Cards shows every Jira story, task and one-issue initiative on the plan as a card. Rows are workstreams in plan order, with cards grouped under their initiative and the rest last. Columns are status (to do, in progress, done, and canceled when you ask) or sprint (earlier, the active one, the next ones, no sprint). Rows can also be people or epics. *Where:* Work, then Cards
- **Filters and honest totals** (Cards). Filter by sprint, person, status, epic or text, or click Mine. Each row and the whole board count cards and estimated points, and say how many aren't estimated, how many you hid, and how many the filters leave out, each on its own. *Where:* Work, then Cards
- **Move a card to place it in the plan** (Cards). Drag a card to another workstream or onto an initiative to place it there, the same way Sort Jira work does, with Undo. Without a mouse, press M on a card, choose the place with the arrow keys, and press Enter. The card glides to where it lands. *Where:* Work, then Cards
- **Move a card across columns to propose a change** (Cards). Dropping a card on another status or sprint doesn't change Jira. It makes a Jira change proposal, and the card shows it as proposed. When a column covers several of your workflow's statuses, you pick which one. Your last pick is remembered. *Where:* Work, then Cards
- **Choose what a card shows** (Cards). Choose the fields a card shows and their order (key, summary, status, assignee, points, sprint, epic, parent, labels, priority, due date, blocked, initiative), compact, normal or detailed, and wider cards for more points. The plan holds the team's layout; you can use your own in this browser, with Reset to the team's layout. *Where:* Settings, then Cards
- **Hide a Jira item, with a reason** (Cards). Hide a card to keep it off the plan's views, with an optional reason. Sightline uses the plan's own ways: a story is switched off in its initiative, an epic is parked, an issue not on the plan is marked not ours. The Hidden list shows how and why, with Bring back. Work that's on the plan as its own task or initiative can't be hidden. *Where:* Work, then Cards, Hidden
- **The assistant can set the card layout and hide items** (Assistant). An assistant can change the team's card layout and hide or bring back Jira items. Each change waits for your review, which says how each item would be hidden, including when hiding parks an epic. *Where:* Assistant, Changes

### Improved

- **Older copies open these plans read-only** (Plan file). A plan with a team card layout or hide reasons opens read-only in an older copy of Sightline, so nothing is lost. Update everyone's copy to edit it. *Where:* Opening a plan

## 1.124.6 · Oct 26, 2026

Days opens and scrolls smoothly in big plans.

### Fixed

- **Days lays out only the rows near the screen** (Performance). The rows near the screen are laid out first and the rest as you scroll to them. In a large plan Days opens in about a third of the time and scrolls smoothly. Every row is still on the page, so finding text and printing work as before. *Where:* Timeline, Days

## 1.124.5 · Oct 26, 2026

Opening and closing an item is quicker.

### Fixed

- **Choosing an item no longer redraws the whole timeline** (Performance). The timeline stays as it is and only the highlight and its links move, so in a large plan opening an item takes about 75% less time and closing it about 85% less. Anything that changes what the timeline shows, like an edit, a filter, a new day or a folded sprint shelf, still redraws it in full. *Where:* Timeline, Weeks and Days

## 1.124.4 · Oct 26, 2026

Sprint presets answer in half the time.

### Fixed

- **Presets draw the timeline once** (Performance). It's drawn once, so in a large plan a preset takes about half as long. The preset is still remembered for your next visit. *Where:* Timeline, the toolbar's 1, 2, 3 and Fit

## 1.124.3 · Oct 26, 2026

The Timeline answers faster with sprint shelves on.

### Fixed

- **Sprint shelves no longer slow every click** (Performance). The shelves work out the sprints once per workstream. In a large plan, Fit and zooming are about 40% faster, This + next about 25%, and opening an item, filtering, Undo and saving about 25 to 30%. The shelves look the same. *Where:* Timeline, in Weeks with sprint shelves on

## 1.124.2 · Oct 26, 2026

Big plans draw faster, Days most of all.

### Fixed

- **Note counts no longer slow every redraw** (Performance). Notes are sorted by item once per redraw. In a large plan, Days opens in about half the time, opening the plan is about 13% faster, and changing the Timeline's zoom, a preset or a filter is about 10% faster. The note counts and badges are the same as before. *Where:* Everywhere items show a note count, most noticeably Days

## 1.124.1 · Oct 25, 2026

The timeline's header is short again.

### Fixed

- **Zoom controls moved to the toolbar** (Timeline). They're one compact group in the toolbar, beside Weeks and Days: ‹ the sprint picker › | 1 2 3 Fit | − +. Tooltips keep the full names and shortcuts, and the picker's tooltip shows the dates on screen. The corner holds just the row label again. *Where:* Timeline, the toolbar

## 1.124.0 · Oct 25, 2026

Jira stories on sprint shelves, sized by points.

### New

- **Sprint shelves for Jira stories** (Timeline). Each workstream's Jira stories sit on a shelf per sprint, grouped under their initiative. A tile's width follows its points, on one scale for the whole chart, and it shows its points, a status symbol, and who has it. Not estimated stories get their own strip, and stories with no sprint are counted as Unscheduled. Nothing in the plan changes. *Where:* Timeline, Weeks, under each workstream
- **Honest shelf summaries** (Timeline). Each shelf sums its stories, estimated points and done points, next to the stories not estimated. It says when filters apply, and that capacity isn't compared yet. *Where:* Timeline, under each sprint's shelf
- **Summaries at Fit, tiles at one sprint** (Timeline). At Fit or several sprints, each shelf shows a short summary. Pick one or two sprints to see the tiles. Show the stories, beside a workstream's shelves, opens or folds them by hand, and that choice is kept in this browser. *Where:* Timeline, the shelf row's label
- **Spotlight one person** (Timeline). Pick a person in Spotlight to light up their tiles across the shelves, with their stories, points and stories not estimated. *Where:* Timeline, the shelf row's label, while the stories show

### Improved

- **Go back to bars if you prefer** (Timeline). Show, then On sprint shelves, turns the shelves off and draws each story as a bar again. Days keeps its story rows either way. *Where:* Timeline, Show

## 1.123.0 · Oct 25, 2026

Size List's columns, and choose which ones wrap.

### New

- **Resize any column** (List). Drag the edge of a column's heading to resize it, or focus the edge and use the arrow keys. Double-click an edge for its default width. Wide tables scroll sideways. *Where:* List, the column headings
- **Choose which columns wrap** (List). Columns, in List's toolbar, sets each column to wrap or keep one line. A one-line column is cut short and shows the full text on hover. Reset columns puts everything back. These settings are yours, in this browser, and printing still shows every column in full. *Where:* List, then Columns

### Fixed

- **Item names are full size** (List). Item names use the same size as the rest of the table, and every cell in a row lines up. *Where:* List, the Item column

## 1.122.0 · Oct 25, 2026

Change a workstream's ID so it says what the workstream is.

### New

- **A workstream's ID can be changed** (Workstreams). Change it in the workstream's panel, under ID. Everything that uses it changes in the same update: work, milestones, notes, meetings, process blocks, deliverables, time splits, guidance, saved views, the baseline, snapshots and the last status update. One Undo puts it all back. *Where:* Click a workstream's name on the Timeline, then ID
- **Assistants can propose an ID change, and you always review it** (Assistant). An assistant can propose a workstream's new ID. It always waits for you, at every review level. A change an assistant wrote before the ID changed still applies: review says it used the old ID. *Where:* The assistant's Changes

### Improved

- **Old IDs keep working** (Plan file). The plan remembers a workstream's old IDs, so files and copies that still use them find it, and an old ID is never given to another workstream. Older versions of Sightline open a plan with a changed ID read-only. *Where:* The plan file

## 1.121.0 · Oct 25, 2026

See one whole sprint, edge to edge, and step sprint by sprint.

### New

- **Fit the view to a sprint** (Timeline). Pick a sprint in the zoom control and the view fits it exactly, from its first day to its last, in Weeks and Days, for sprints of any length. The arrows and [ and ] step whole sprints, and . goes to the sprint we're in. Show two or more sprints with + and −. The choice stays in this browser and links carry it. *Where:* Timeline, the zoom control at the top left
- **One click to this sprint, the next two, or the next three** (Timeline). This sprint, This + next, Next 3 and Fit sit beside the sprint picker, each fitted from the sprint we're in (or the next one, between sprints). Shift+1, Shift+2, Shift+3 and Shift+0 do the same. A plan with sprints opens on This + next the first time, then on your last choice. A link with a sprint still wins. *Where:* Timeline, the zoom control at the top left

## 1.120.3 · Oct 25, 2026

Milestone and gate labels that fall close together stay readable.

### Fixed

- **Labels close together no longer run into each other** (Timeline). Labels are spaced by their real width at the chart's current zoom, width and text size, and spaced again when any of those change. A workstream's milestones use three rows at most; past that, a label is cut short where the next one starts, keeping its date, and shows in full when you hover over it or tab to it. Gates whose markers would touch share one flag, with a count. *Where:* Timeline, Weeks

## 1.120.2 · Oct 25, 2026

Install Sightline with npm.

### Improved

- **One command to install** (Install). npx @troylar/sightline install <folder> puts the app, the planning skills and an invented example plan in a new folder. The README and the availability page explain each install route. *Where:* README, and docs/availability.md
- **Neutral wording for any assistant** (Assistant). The instructions the app gives your AI assistant use a generic source name and batch id in their example. Any assistant's name is still accepted and shown as written. *Where:* Roadmap, Assistant amendments

### Fixed

- **Helpers match the app they came with** (Install). sightline helpers points to helpers stamped with the app's version, the same files the app and its download carry. *Where:* npx @troylar/sightline helpers

An update that keeps being overwritten no longer saves over and over.

A file that still holds exactly what you saved is never saved again. *Where:* Any quick update to a shared plan

Assistant changes apply whole, or say why not.

Your assistant proposes where Jira work goes.

Stories: the why behind each item.

The whole forecast in one place.

People rows draw their work again, and the assistant scripts travel with the page.

## 1.105.0 · Oct 25, 2026

Why an initiative finishes when it does, and who the work waits for.

### New

- **Follow the chain that sets a finish date** (Forecast). An initiative's card has a "Why it finishes then" list. It walks back through what held the initiative up: the work it waited for, and the work that had or shared its people, each with dates, until it reaches the first day, a gate, a Jira sprint or a workstream's start. *Where:* Initiative card, under the forecast dates (open "Why it finishes then")

## 1.104.0 · Oct 24, 2026

A forecast date on every initiative, with the reason for it.

### New

- **See when an initiative is likely to finish** (Forecast). An initiative with an effort shows its forecast on its card: the likely start and finish, and the finish if everything takes its high estimate. Sightline works it out day by day from who's in each workstream, their time, holidays and time off, what each item waits for, and the other work competing for the same people. It never moves anything on the timeline. *Where:* The initiative card, under Effort left
- **Know why a date is what it is** (Forecast). The forecast says what set an item's start: the item it waited for, a gate, a Jira issue's sprint, or the work its people were on, with dates. It also gives the pace in person-weeks a week and who's on it. *Where:* The initiative card
- **No date, with the reason, when the forecast can't give one** (Forecast). An item gets no date, never a guess, when it waits for something with no effort, sits on a dependency loop, is in a workstream with nobody in it, or waits for a Jira issue with no sprint. The card says which one, and anything waiting on it says so too. *Where:* The initiative card
- **Holders show their latest finish** (Forecast). An initiative with others inside shows the forecast finish of the last of them, or how many have no date yet. *Where:* The card of an initiative with others inside

Capacity day by day, the second step toward a forecast.

- **Split someone's time across workstreams** (Forecast). For someone in two or more workstreams, the person card has Time split: a weight for each workstream. With no split, their time divides evenly. When a workstream ends, its share moves to their other workstreams. *Where:* The person card, Time split
- **Keep time back for support and unplanned work** (Forecast). Set a reserve for the team in Team, and a different one for any workstream on its card. The workstream card shows this week's capacity for planned work, in person-weeks, after the reserve. *Where:* Team, Reserve; the workstream card
- **Your assistant can set capacity inputs** (Assistant). Assistant changes can set when someone joins or leaves, how their time splits across workstreams, and the team's or a workstream's reserve. *Where:* Assistant changes

- **Older copies open a plan with these settings read-only** (Plan file). A plan with join or leave dates, time splits or reserves opens read-only in copies older than 1.103.0, so they can't save over them. *Where:* Opening a plan in an older copy

Effort estimates, the first step toward a forecast.

The card says what the forecast will do with it: Forecast, Fixed (Jira's sprint sets its dates), Not counted (no effort yet, which is never treated as zero), or Out of scope if you tick Leave out of the forecast. - **Undo kept as change records** (Saving). Undo used to keep a full copy of the plan for every step; older steps are now kept as the few hundred bytes that undo them, so a long editing session uses a fraction of the memory. Each step is checked when it's stored; the rare one that can't be described that way keeps its copy, so undo and redo are always exact. *Where:* Undo and Redo.
- **Bigger changes stay undoable from Activity** (Plan). Activity's Undo this now works for changes up to 96 KB (it was 16 KB), which covers a large Apply of assistant amendments. Anything bigger is listed as too big to undo from there, instead of the undo quietly disappearing. *Where:* Manage, Activity.

## 1.62.1 · Sep 28, 2026

Senior review 13: amendments you can rely on.

### Fixed

- **Amendments keep working** (Views). An amendments file that hadn't changed stopped working after its next 30-second check; it now stays loaded. Reads don't overlap, a file that's too big is refused before it's read, and switching plans drops the other plan's file. *Where:* Roadmap, Assistant amendments.
- **Hostile input is refused** (Saving). Amendment files can't use names that would change how the page works (like __proto__), odd values are refused rather than coerced, and link limits are enforced. Invalid wins over changed since. An add for an existing item must match everything it sets. Receipts follow what a change says, so an undone or rewritten change shows as Ready again. *Where:* Assistant amendments.
- **One set of rules** (Views). Amendments now follow the same rules as editing a card: a target makes an idea Planned, no timing makes it an idea again, a release sets the quarter, and new wording needs approving again. Jira proposals from amendments record Jira's current value and use sprint and assignee ids, so they don't look stale at once. *Where:* Assistant amendments; Roadmap.
- **Release notes and pull requests** (Views). Approvals are protected from older copies (they open the plan read-only), approval needs customer wording, and Markdown notes keep names as text. Merged pull requests are those updated this sprint, and a sprint with none says so. The export leaves notes out, lists linked Jira work first and says what it left out, and is there before a file is connected. *Where:* A release's card; Sprint; Assistant amendments.

Safer undo, one editor per tab, nothing lost from the sprint list.

Plan format checks and a better Standup.

Safer saves and hides.

Cards that show what's Jira's and what's the plan's.

Hide what someone added, and undo one change.

See who added what, and what changed.

Groundwork: safer saves across versions, bigger plans.

- **Drag milestones, gates and notes** (Timeline). Drag them along their row to another day. A click still opens them. A milestone that follows initiatives says so instead of moving. *Where:* Timeline, Days and Weeks.

See what comes from Jira, and what was added here.

- **From Jira and Added here look different** (Timeline). What comes from Jira is outlined in its workstream's color, with its Jira key. What was added here stays filled. This holds in Weeks, Days and the people rows, for initiatives, tasks and stories. The key explains both. *Where:* Timeline.

A line under the controls says how many items added here are hidden, with Show everyone. Each plan remembers its own choice in your browser, and a saved view can keep it. *Where:* Timeline.

### Improved

- **Jira's sprints and the plan's own timeboxes** (Sprints). When the plan follows Jira's sprints, a timebox the plan added (after Jira's last sprint, say) shows in italics. Hovering a Jira sprint shows Jira's exact dates. *Where:* Timeline sprint headers.
- **Parked initiatives are counted** (Timeline). A line says how many are parked, with a link to Plan, then Epics. *Where:* Timeline.

Undo quick updates, and groups that stay open.

Redo puts it back, and a toast after each decision offers Undo. The Undo button names what it will undo. *Where:* Plan, then Epics; the initiative and story cards.
- **Epics groups stay the way you left them** (Jira). Each group remembers being opened or closed. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.

The weeks before Jira's first sprint say so, with a note on how to start the plan there instead. *Where:* Settings, then Jira, then Sprints from Jira.

Finished epics stay out of your way.

### New

An epic whose stories are all done or abandoned goes into a closed Finished in Jira group: it isn't in Unsorted, isn't counted as to sort, and isn't touched by Park all. A new epic with no stories yet stays in Unsorted. Each row says how many stories are open. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.
- **Park finished epics in one click** (Jira). When epics on the board are finished in Jira, Epics says how many and offers Park N finished. It keeps their initiatives and notes, and takes them off the timeline. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.

Epics on the board are counted first (with their stories listed), then the other epics your searches found (counted only), all within the same 5,000-story limit. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py and run install again. *Where:* sightline-jira-sync.py.

Sorting that respects your picks, and a lighter page.

See whether Jira is keeping up.

When a watch is more than twice its interval late, the page says so and what to check: that the computer running it is on and signed in. It updates every minute while the page is open. *Where:* Plan, then Epics; and Settings.

Stories: counts that agree, and switches that stick.

When you open the page, the status line says Jira is paused until you reconnect. Plan opens on Epics for plans that use Jira. Your browser may offer to allow the folder on every visit, so you won't be asked again. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.

An epic's stories, inside its initiative.

Stories have a dashed outline and their Jira key. Click one for its card. They're read-only, so change them in Jira. Off for now hides a story from the timeline and from progress, without changing Jira. Anyone can do it without Start editing, and two people's changes both count. Everyone should use this version, because older copies drop the list when they save. *Where:* The initiative's card, or the story's card.

- **The sync lists each epic's stories** (Jira sync). For epics on the board, the status file lists up to 3,000 stories with their sprint and status. Parked epics are counted but not listed. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py and run install again. *Where:* sightline-jira-sync.py.

## 1.13.1 · Sep 26, 2026

Epic decisions that stick, and a sync that keeps going.

### Fixed

- **Park means parked** (Jira). Each epic belongs to one initiative, however it was linked. Park and Park all switch it off everywhere, and On… won't make a second initiative for an epic that's already on the board. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.
- **Messages say what really happened** (Jira). If it didn't save, your picks stay. In an editing session it says the change waits for Save. Back on explains when the epic's initiative was removed. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.

- **watch keeps going** (Jira sync). A failure is reported for that plan only and retried after a minute, then less often. Only one watch runs on a computer, and one that loses the lock stops. *Where:* sightline-jira-sync.py watch.
- **sync --save changes only what you give it** (Jira sync). Each option replaces just that setting, and settings are saved only after a sync works. When several searches fill the file, the later ones say they were skipped. *Where:* sightline-jira-sync.py sync.

Jira keeps itself in sync, and every project carries its own jira folder.

The planner gets a name.

### New

- **Meet Sightline** (What's new). The planner is now called Sightline: your team's work, in plain sight. *Where:* The top left of the page and the browser tab.
- **One plan file your whole team shares** (Saving). Link a plan file your team shares. One person edits at a time, anyone can make quick updates, and nothing is overwritten without a backup. *Where:* File, then Link a file.
- **Your plan by lane or by person** (Timeline). See work by lane or by person, zoom from weeks to days, and plan around holidays and time off. *Where:* The Timeline and People tabs.
- **Sprints, meetings, and team rhythms** (Sprints & process). Set up sprints, repeating meetings, and process blocks like code freezes and releases that repeat every sprint from a rule. *Where:* Plan, then Sprints.
- **Jira status next to your plan** (Jira). Show each item's Jira status beside it. A small script fetches it, so the page never sees your token. *Where:* File, then Jira status.
